title: Lattice refinement of a cubic box, Bragg peaks with nbraggup = nq
purpose: Exercises the cubic branch of the lattice refinement and of the Bragg-peak calculation of the `epsr` engine [@soper1996,@soper2005,@epsrmanual], with a Q range of the Bragg calculation that is limited by the number of Q points.
system: A molecular crystal of DMSO and water: a cubic 6.84 Å unit cell with 2 DMSO + 4 water molecules (from `mixato`, `randomise` and 200 Monte Carlo cycles of `epsr` with `potfac 0`), replicated with `makelatticeato` 4 × 4 × 4 into a cubic 27.36 Å box (384 molecules, 2048 atoms, 300 K). The atom types are those of EPSR-test, so its `.pcof`, weights and three D-DMSO/water neutron data files are used unchanged; for the crystal they are numerical input only, not a physical model of measured data. For a crystal the simulation box holds only a few unit cells, so the Bragg part of the structure factor [@squires1978] is computed from the reciprocal lattice: intensities per atom pair and reflection are broadened into peaks, divided by the number of unit cells, damped by a Debye-Waller factor and replace the intermolecular partial S(Q) up to `qbraggmax`. Gaussian peaks, no broadening below 0.5 1/Å, Debye-Waller parameter 0.05.
inputs: `scripts/make_case.sh` regenerates the inputs (verified byte-identical). Keywords changed: `nq 100` (Q up to 5 1/Å), `iinit 1`, `ntimes 2`, `qwidthqmax 0.01 4.5`, `mplicities 4 4 4`, `hklqmin 0.5 5.0 0.05`, `nlatrefine 2`, `latrefine 0.3 0 0 0 0 0`. `commands.txt`: `repeat 2`.
verification: `nbraggup` is limited to `nq` ((4.5 + 3/5)/0.05 + 1 = 103 > 100). In the cubic branch one `ran1` call changes a (b = c = a, angles 90°); the trial change is undone exactly by the constant-density rescaling, so the fit does not change and every trial is accepted; on the last step `ilatrefine` is advanced to skip the recomputation. This is the Fortran behaviour and it is reproduced.
